title: Elementary Differential Geometry
notes: Open by presenting the chapter as the grammar used by the rest of the course. The lecture starts with charts and smooth functions, then adds tensor calculus, smooth maps, connections, exponential maps, curvature, and the special rigidity of totally geodesic submanifolds.

title: The Chapter Builds A Machine
notes: Use this route slide to prevent the long source span from feeling like a list of definitions. Each row adds one operation that was unavailable before it, and the final rows explain why curvature and geodesic behavior become invariant tests rather than coordinate artifacts.

title: Smooth Structure Is Compatible Local Data
notes: Emphasize that a manifold is not merely a set with coordinates. The important condition is compatibility on overlaps, because that lets local calculations glue into globally meaningful smooth functions, vector fields, tensors, and later partitions of unity.

title: Partitions Of Unity Turn Local Work Global
notes: Connect the bump-function picture to the chapter's technical hypotheses. Once locally finite weights sum to one, local formulas can be patched without losing smoothness. That is the hidden infrastructure behind metrics, connections, and global tensor fields.

title: Tangent Vectors Are Derivations
notes: Frame tangent vectors as operators before drawing arrows. The derivation viewpoint explains why the same vector can be recognized in every chart: it differentiates smooth functions and obeys the product rule, while coordinates only provide one basis for recording it.

title: Forms And Pullbacks Preserve Alternation
notes: The point of this slide is algebraic hygiene. Forms measure oriented infinitesimal content, exterior differentiation records antisymmetric change, and pullback moves forms backward through a map so integration and orientation can be discussed on the source.

title: Mappings Are Measured By Their Differentials
notes: Make the differential the central inspection tool. A smooth map can bend a grid globally, but at one point it is read by a linear map on tangent spaces. Rank, kernel, image, and Jacobian sign are the local evidence for regularity.

title: Constant Rank Gives Local Normal Form
notes: Use the three examples as mental models for the constant-rank theorem. Immersions look locally like embeddings of active coordinates, submersions look like projections, and level sets become submanifolds when the differential has the expected rank.

title: A Connection Chooses How To Differentiate
notes: Stress that ordinary derivatives of vector fields subtract vectors living in different tangent spaces. A connection supplies the comparison rule. Torsion and metric compatibility are then extra properties of that rule, with the Levi-Civita connection occupying the Riemannian sweet spot.

title: Parallelism And Geodesics Come From One Rule
notes: Parallel transport and geodesics should be presented as two uses of the same covariant derivative. A transported vector has zero derivative along the curve, while a geodesic transports its own velocity. The equation is local, but the geometric meaning is intrinsic.

title: The Exponential Map Packages Geodesic Initial Data
notes: Describe the exponential map as a controlled conversion from tangent vectors to nearby manifold points. Near zero it gives normal coordinates, and within a convex normal neighborhood it makes short geodesics unique. Later curvature controls how far this picture remains reliable.

title: Moving Frames Expose Torsion And Curvature
notes: This is where the chapter's tensor notation becomes compact. A coframe and connection forms encode differentiation without permanent coordinates. Cartan's first structural equation records torsion, and the second records curvature as the failure of connection forms to close flatly.

title: Curvature Measures Failed Return
notes: Use the loop diagram to give curvature a tactile meaning. If a vector is parallel transported around a tiny loop and fails to return exactly to itself, the leading error is governed by the curvature tensor on the two-plane spanned by the loop directions.

title: Constant Curvature Controls Radial Spread
notes: The comparison formulas give students a quantitative sign check. Positive curvature squeezes radial circles and small disk area compared with Euclidean space, while negative curvature expands them. This is the computational bridge to the notebook's curvature-sign lab.

title: Negative Curvature Has Global Consequences
notes: Treat the negative-curvature results as a chain of consequences driven by expansion transverse to radial geodesics. Under the stated completeness and simply connected hypotheses, no conjugate points and the global behavior of the exponential map become much more rigid.

title: Totally Geodesic Means Ambient Geodesics Stay Inside
notes: Distinguish intrinsic geodesic behavior from the stronger ambient condition. A submanifold is totally geodesic only when geodesics initially tangent to it remain tangent in the ambient manifold. The equator and latitude contrast gives a compact diagnostic.

title: Notebook Diagnostics As Lecture Evidence
notes: Close by tying the slide chain to the notebook checks. The computational artifacts are not decorative; they verify partition sums, exterior-calculus identities, map regularity, exponential-map behavior, curvature comparisons, and the equator-versus-latitude totally geodesic test.
